title: AMD shares its third quarter results today after the close
summary: AMD said it would report third quarter results on Tuesday, November 3, after the market closes, with a call at 5 p.m. Eastern. In its last report the company said it expected about $13 billion in sales this quarter, give or take $300 million.
why: A company's own forecast is a yardstick. When the real numbers come out, investors compare them with that range and with what they hoped for. A stock can fall even on good results if people hoped for more, so a big move in either direction is possible.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield eased to 4.91%
summary: Treasury data show the 10 year yield closed Monday at 4.91%, down from 5.05% on October 28. The yield is the interest rate the government pays to borrow money for ten years.
why: This rate is like a price tag on money. When it falls, safer investments pay a bit less, so investors may feel more comfortable owning stocks, especially fast growing ones. When it rises, the opposite can happen.
source: U.S. Treasury daily yield curve rates

title: The Treasury announces how much it plans to borrow on Wednesday
summary: The U.S. Treasury is scheduled to announce its quarterly refunding plan on Wednesday, November 4. This tells the market how much government debt it plans to sell in the coming months.
why: When the government sells more bonds, it can push interest rates up, because buyers want to be paid for taking on more supply. Rates matter to every stock, so people watch this announcement closely.

title: Tech was the weakest part of the Nasdaq on Monday
summary: Sector data for the Nasdaq show technology companies fell about 3.5% on average on Monday, while consumer defensive companies, which sell everyday products, rose about 2.4%. On our list AMD fell 7.5% and Microsoft fell 2.8%.
why: Stocks in the same industry often move together, so a bad day for one can pull others down. That is why spreading money across different kinds of businesses can make a rough day feel smaller.
